FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Numbers 1–10 Flashcards

Ten counting cards, one for every number from 1 to 10. Big numerals, number words and friendly pictures to count together — pick a card, count slowly and stop whenever your preschooler has had enough.

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Read every card right here.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Counting to three is a whole lesson

    At three, a calm count to three with pointing is real maths. You do not need all ten cards in one sitting — one, two and five are plenty for a first day.

  2. 02

    Point at every single thing

    The heart of counting is one number per object. Point to each apple, duck or butterfly as you say its number, and go slowly enough for your child to see the rule.

  3. 03

    Start with your child’s favourite picture

    Ducks, cars, balloons — let your child pick the card. Counting a picture they love holds attention twice as long as counting the “right” next number.

  4. 04

    Give today’s number a home

    Tape the card of the day to the fridge at your child’s eye level. Passing it again and again, and counting it once more, is quietly powerful practice.

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS 1–10 · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Number 1 Flashcard — One Apple for Preschoolers

      The first counting card starts with something your child already owns: one shiny apple. Before children count groups, they learn to notice single things — one nose, one cup, one you. This card makes “one” feel like a discovery, not a lesson.

      Teaching tips

      What this number card does

      Turns the very first number into something your child can hold, tap and claim.

      Count it for real

      Give one biscuit, wait for the announcement, then ask how many are left.

      What it teaches

      That a single thing deserves a number of its very own.

      Print it like this

      Tape it low on the fridge, right at small grabbing height.

      Grown-up tip

      Whisper "one" at single things today; quiet words make children lean in.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Numbers & Counting 1–10 for 3 Year Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS 1–10 · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Number 2 Flashcard — Two Ducks for Preschoolers

      Two yellow ducks, side by side and ready to count. Two is where counting finds its rhythm — one, then the other — and pointing at each duck once while saying the number is the classic first count for a reason.

      Teaching tips

      What this number card does

      Gives a name to the pairs your child already wears, eats and trips over.

      Count it for real

      Set two places at the toy table, counting each cup as it lands.

      What it teaches

      One-to-one correspondence: one number spoken for one thing touched.

      Print it like this

      Print on card stock — this one will get carried everywhere.

      Grown-up tip

      Tap each item as you say its number; taps keep counts honest.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS 1–10 · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Number 3 Flashcard — Three Cats for Preschoolers

      Three orange cats — two sitting up top, one below. Three is small enough to count at a glance but big enough to feel like proper counting, and for a three-year-old, being “three cats” is a very good joke indeed.

      Teaching tips

      What this number card does

      Sits at the sweet spot where counting starts to feel like real work.

      Count it for real

      Line up three teddies for a story and count the audience before you begin.

      What it teaches

      Counting small groups without losing track — or giggling too hard.

      Print it like this

      Go big: A4 for the number that loves an audience.

      Grown-up tip

      Stop at three, even mid-plea; a clean finish beats wandering.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS 1–10 · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Number 4 Flashcard — Four Cars for Preschoolers

      Four little blue cars parked in a neat square. Vehicles are dependable favourites, and the two-by-two arrangement makes counting kind: two on top, two below, nothing hiding and nothing crowded.

      Teaching tips

      What this number card does

      Matches a numeral to the fours underfoot — table legs, dog paws, chair feet.

      Count it for real

      Ask for four books for bedtime and count them onto the pillow together.

      What it teaches

      That numbers name real groups, not just sounds in a song.

      Print it like this

      Print two copies so this number can live in two rooms.

      Grown-up tip

      Body-count it: four jumps to the door beat a quiet quiz.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS 1–10 · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Number 5 Flashcard — Five Ladybugs for Preschoolers

      Five red ladybugs in two friendly rows. Five is the hand number — a whole hand of fingers — which makes it the natural finish line for a first counting session, and a very satisfying one to reach.

      Teaching tips

      What this number card does

      Puts a number on the hand your child already waves, grabs and counts with.

      Count it for real

      Count down from five to start any race, dinner or spaghetti-blowing contest.

      What it teaches

      Finger counting — a built-in number line your child never leaves at home.

      Print it like this

      Stick it by the sink, where hands get washed and counted.

      Grown-up tip

      Hide a hand behind your back and ask what went missing.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS 1–10 · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Number 6 Flashcard — Six Stars for Preschoolers

      Six smiling yellow stars in two rows of three. Six is the first number past a whole hand, and the tidy two-rows layout invites the loveliest trick in early counting: three, then three more.

      Teaching tips

      What this number card does

      Stretches counting past one hand, which is exactly where it gets interesting.

      Count it for real

      Bake six biscuits and let the counter guard them until tea.

      What it teaches

      Counting groups bigger than a glance — and patience while the count finishes.

      Print it like this

      Cheap paper is fine; scribble tally marks around the edge.

      Grown-up tip

      Count in threes with a pause after three; six likes company.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS 1–10 · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Number 7 Flashcard — Seven Flowers for Preschoolers

      Seven pink flowers scattered across a wide card. Seven is famously the wobbly count — the jump past five trips up almost every little counter — so this card rewards going slowly more than any other.

      Teaching tips

      What this number card does

      Makes the wobbliest numeral in the bunch friendly, familiar and countable.

      Count it for real

      Seven buttons into the jar before bath; drop and count, one by one.

      What it teaches

      Careful counting past five, where little eyes and fingers start to race.

      Print it like this

      A5 fits the bathroom door, home of teeth-counting o'clock.

      Grown-up tip

      If the count tangles, shrug and start again from one, no fuss.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS 1–10 · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Number 8 Flashcard — Eight Frogs for Preschoolers

      Eight green frogs in two tidy rows of four. The neat grid is a gift for young counters: count one row, count the other row, and suddenly eight does not feel nearly as big as it sounds.

      Teaching tips

      What this number card does

      Shows that numbers keep going after your hand runs out of fingers.

      Count it for real

      Lay the table for eight toys and count chairs, plates and empty seats.

      What it teaches

      Holding a count together as it grows — six, seven, eight, steady.

      Print it like this

      Thick paper, please; a number this big deserves something sturdy.

      Grown-up tip

      Ease up for the last two; the finish is where counts slip.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS 1–10 · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Number 9 Flashcard — Nine Balloons for Preschoolers

      Nine red balloons in three neat columns of three. Nine is the last stop before ten, and this tidy layout is perfect for spotting little groups inside a big count — three rows make nine feel friendly.

      Teaching tips

      What this number card does

      Walks your child to the edge of ten, the number every counter is aiming for.

      Count it for real

      Gather nine leaves on the walk home, counting each one into the pocket.

      What it teaches

      That each number has neighbours — and nine sits right beside ten.

      Print it like this

      Keep a spare in the change bag for café-table counting.

      Grown-up tip

      Backwards counting from nine turns tidy-up time into a landing game.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · NUMBERS 1–10 · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Number 10 Flashcard — Ten Butterflies for Preschoolers

      Ten blue butterflies in two rows of five — a whole counting kingdom, and the finish line of the set. Reaching ten together deserves a drumroll, or at the very least a happy wiggle.

      Teaching tips

      What this number card does

      Delivers the big one: all ten fingers, counted and finally claimed.

      Count it for real

      Ten jumps before bath, counted loudly; wobble on purpose at the last one.

      What it teaches

      Two hands of counting — the base of all the maths to come.

      Print it like this

      Laminate it — a finish line this important should be wipe-clean.

      Grown-up tip

      Celebrate a full ten with one victory lap around the kitchen table.

      Teach it, step by step
